clue.text: Displays variety of gins Gretchen has drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the words are reeling about, so their letters are mixed up anew

explanation.surface: Gretchen has downed a whole assortment of gins and shows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges GINS GRETCHEN HAS; 'has' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring the changes is an idiom for introducing variation, taken from bell-ringing sequences.

clue.text: Cub reporter's buttocks clenching heartless Arab's 1 part 1

parts.note: Tintin is the boy reporter of Hergé's comic books

indicators.note: clenching means the buttocks word grips the next piece inside it

parts.note: nates is the anatomical Latin word for buttocks

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the name is removed

parts.note: Abdul is a common Arab name

explanation.surface: A young reporter tenses his backside around an Arab's shrunken form.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 part 1' means the first part of 1 Down, the word for what bells do. 'heartless' leaves ABUL, which the buttocks clench.
explanation.definitionFit: To tintinnabulate is to ring or tinkle like a bell, a sense matching the first word of 1 Down.

clue.text: Sage carrying king up hollow apple tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the assembled piece is read from bottom to top
carrying means the wise man holds the king inside

parts.note: a magus is a wise man, as in the three Magi
R abbreviates rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: hollow means the centre of the fruit word is taken out

explanation.surface: A herb is laden with a monarch and set atop an apple tree with no core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the sage-and-king piece upwards, giving SUGARM; 'hollow' takes just the central letter of the fruit, leaving APLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar maple is a North American tree whose sap gives maple syrup.

clue.text: Cautious about companion's lasciviousness

indicators.note: about means the wary word goes round the companion piece

parts.note: leery means wary or cautious
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of their partner's lustful tendencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lechery is excessive sexual desire, a synonym for lasciviousness.

clue.text: Zest for dance with nothing wanting

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the zero is dropped from the dance

parts.note: the tango is a ballroom dance
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone shows enthusiasm for dancing though they have nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a sharp, lively flavour, much the same as zest.

clue.text: Poet (Her Majesty's jester) in banjo performance

indicators.note: a performance on the banjo suggests the letters played in a new arrangement

parts.note: HM is the standard abbreviation for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: The monarch's jester gives a banjo recital.
explanation.walkthrough: HM plus JESTER IN BANJO is rearranged by 'performance'. The bracket nods to the poet as Laureate, the Queen's court versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Betjeman was an English poet and Poet Laureate from 1972 to 1984.

clue.text: 6's Pavlovian response to 1 part 1?

parts.note: Pavlov's dogs answered a bell; the clue imagines the poet at 6 Down called by ringing, which is also the title of his verse autobiography

explanation.walkthrough: '1 part 1' is RINGS, the first part of 1 Down; 6 Down is Betjeman. Pavlov trained dogs to respond to a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Betjeman's 1960 blank-verse autobiography, and literally what a bell-conditioned subject responds to.

clue.text: Make fun of law officers I backed to break law

indicators.note: to break means to split the law word open and sit inside it

parts.note: a rule is a law or regulation

indicators.note: backed means the officers and the I are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police officers and I go backwards to break the law, and are mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the officers and I round, giving IDIC, set inside the law word by 'to break'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule someone is to mock them, the same as making fun of them.

clue.text: Bad feeling caused by game down under?

definitions.text: Bad feeling caused by game down under?

parts.words: Bad feeling caused by game down under?
parts.note: the game down under is the emu, an Australian bird; the phrase 'an emu's' said quickly gives a word for hostility

explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means wild creatures hunted for food, and 'down under' means Australia; the question mark flags the pun on how 'an emu's' sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus means hostility or ill will, a bad feeling towards someone.

clue.text: Woman's cry of delight about gun

indicators.note: about means the exclamation wraps round the gun

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of triumph or delight
gat is old American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A woman gives a delighted shout about a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link word ('is').
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's first name, as in Agatha Christie.

clue.text: Doomed man's destiny in field event

definitions.meaning: someone 'for the' this is facing severe punishment, originally the gallows
an athletic event in which competitors leap over a raised bar

explanation.definitionFit: Being for this is an idiom for facing punishment, and it is also an athletics field event.

clue.text: Boy's time in hospital

indicators.note: in means the time letter sits inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

explanation.surface: A boy spends some time in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link word ('is').
explanation.definitionFit: Stan is a boy's name, short for Stanley.

clue.text: Drink to old chairman installing new chairs, perhaps

indicators.note: installing means the chairman takes the mixed letters inside

parts.note: Mao Zedong was Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters given might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Hand a drink to the old chairman who is putting in new chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' mixes N with the chairs into RASCHIN, which 'installing' sets inside the old Chinese leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a cherry liqueur, a type of drink.

clue.text: Release small amount of cash for animal (unusually)

parts.note: to spring a prisoner is to release them
a buck is a dollar, a modest sum

explanation.surface: Freeing a little money for a beast, which is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: '(unusually)' marks that this is a rarer spelling of the antelope more often written springbok.
explanation.definitionFit: The springbuck is a southern African antelope, so it is an animal.

clue.text: State returned representatives given makeovers

indicators.note: returned means the stating word comes back reversed

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
MPs are Members of Parliament, elected representatives

explanation.surface: A state sent back its representatives after giving them makeovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AVER into REVA.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or give a new look, so revamps means gives makeovers.

clue.text: Lover of ladies is in the same place, being stuck in traffic

indicators.note: being stuck in means the abbreviation is lodged inside the trade word

parts.note: traffic means trade or dealing
ib is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place

explanation.surface: A ladies' man stays put, stuck in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribade is a dated term for a lesbian, a woman who loves women.

clue.text: Heterogeneous little item of home entertainment reflected on language

indicators.note: reflected means the short video word is mirrored

parts.note: vid is a short form of video
Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: A small home video reflects on language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next. 'reflected' mirrors the short video word.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means varied or of different kinds, the same as heterogeneous.

clue.text: Like the old poet or martial artist to take over melody and money of yore

indicators.note: to take means the artist's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Jackie Chan is a martial-arts film star

indicators.note: over means the tune and the coin are turned round

parts.note: an air is a melody
the ecu was an old French coin

explanation.surface: A kung fu star takes over a tune and some antique money, in the style of medieval verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the tune and the coin round, giving UCERIA, which the film star 'to take' holds inside. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucerian describes something resembling the work of Geoffrey Chaucer, the medieval English poet.

clue.text: Nameless awards for fiddles

indicators.note: Nameless says N, standing for name, is missing from the awards

parts.note: the Tonys are American theatre awards

explanation.surface: Unnamed prizes are given for violins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to fiddle with it idly, so toys means fiddles.

clue.text: Get into a muddle with e-books on fish

parts.note: E plus NT, the New Testament, a collection of books
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone using e-books about fishing gets confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to twist together or embroil, so to get into a muddle.

clue.text: Crowd barrier

definitions.meaning: the number of spectators at a sporting event
a hinged barrier in a fence or wall

explanation.definitionFit: A gate is the attendance at a match, and also a hinged barrier.

clue.text: Bishops taking sheep for drink producer

indicators.note: taking means the bishops hold the sheep inside

parts.note: B is bishop in chess notation and RR is Right Reverend, the title of bishops
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Bishops take in a sheep in place of a drinks maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer makes beer, so is a producer of drink.

clue.text: Co-religionists adopting railroad of choice

indicators.note: adopting means the sect takes the railroad in

parts.note: a sect is a group sharing a religion
the El is the elevated railroad in Chicago and formerly New York

explanation.surface: A religious group adopts the railway of its choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Select means chosen with care, the pick, so of choice.

clue.text: Friendly Islands hold one back

indicators.note: back means the whole run of islands and numeral is read in reverse
hold means the two islands contain the numeral between them

parts.note: Elba is a Mediterranean island off Tuscany
Cos is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The Friendly Islands keep one at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendly Islands' looks like the Tonga group, but 'Friendly' is the definition. 'hold' gives ELBAICOS, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable means friendly and eager for company.
